title: Singapore University of Social Sciences Bill
what_it_is: Singapore University of Social Sciences Bill

sections.label: Rising percentage targets by year
sections.summary: The percentage rises from 20% in 2000 to 35% this year, and will reach 40% by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It stands at 35% this year and will be further raised to 40% by 2020.

sections.label: Sixth AU Singapore University Social Sciences
sections.summary: Passing this Bill sets up a sixth AU, the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: With the passing of this Bill, we will set up a sixth AU, the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS).

sections.label: SIM University restructured and renamed
sections.summary: The Government decided to restructure SIM University into an AU and renamed it SUSS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Government has decided to restructure SIM University into an AU, and renamed it SUSS.

sections.label: SIM Endowment Fund in SUSS
sections.summary: An endowment fund named the SIM Endowment Fund will be set up in SUSS to build capability and support lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In recognition of SIM's contributions to the setting up and development of SUSS, an endowment fund will be set up in SUSS, named the SIM Endowment Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Fund will be used to build SUSS' capability, support the activities of the university and ensure that individuals continue to have access to lifelong learning opportunities through scholarships, sponsorships and study awards.

sections.label: Government support and strategic guidance for SUSS
sections.summary: It signals Government support for SUSS and empowers the Government to guide its strategic development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: First, it signals the Government's support for SUSS and assures the public of SUSS' credibility and standing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Second, it empowers the Government to better guide the strategic development of SUSS towards meeting national objectives in education as well as economic and social development.

sections.label: Admission consideration for working people
sections.summary: MOE is asked to consider special admission consideration for working people with workplace experience, internships or SkillsFuture Earn and Learn experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For working people, I hope that MOE will consider how, at the enrolment phase, to allow working people with workplace experience to be given special consideration when enrolling in a university place in SUSS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Furthermore, for those of them who have participated in internship programmes, or those who have acquired experience in the SkillsFuture Earn and Learn programme, that these be considered additional admission points when they are applying for a place in the university.

sections.label: Suggested applied social sciences content
sections.summary: The speaker suggests adding counselling, coaching, organisation behaviour, clinical psychology, data analytics, consumer behaviour and labour management relations beyond social work, early childhood and HR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On the Minister's note about Applied Social Sciences, I would like to suggest that we could also ensure that beyond social work, early childhood and HR, there could be other applied contents, such as counselling, coaching, organisation behaviour, clinical psychology, data analytics, consumer behaviour and even labour management relations to complement HR content.

sections.label: Graduate employment rate yardstick
sections.summary: The speaker notes the graduate employment rate is 90% after six months but hopes it is not the only yardstick.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Whilst our graduate employment rate remains healthy at 90% after six months of graduation, I hope that we do not see that as the only yardstick.

sections.label: SIM University renaming
sections.summary: The speaker was surprised by the renaming of SIM University as the Singapore University of Social Sciences, calling it a significant reorientation as it becomes the sixth autonomous university.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, as a social scientist by vocation, I was pleasantly surprised that the Government announced the renaming of SIM University as the Singapore University of Social Sciences.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is, of course, not a simple renaming, but a significant reorientation of Singapore's leading private university catering to adult education as it comes under public stewardship to become our sixth AU.

sections.label: Risk of research arm
sections.summary: The speaker states the risk that a university dedicated to applied social sciences could become a mere research arm for the Civil Service.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The risk involved in the setting up of a whole university dedicated to applied social sciences is that the university could become a mere research arm for the Civil Service.

sections.label: Worry about silo universities
sections.summary: The speaker worries higher education will evolve into six functionally differentiated silo universities that do not relate to each other.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: My worry is that our higher education field will evolve into six silo universities, all functionally differentiated and not relating to each, each becoming a great echo chamber in itself, six blind men feeling the different parts to know the strange elephant.

sections.label: Research grants and impact measures
sections.summary: The speaker says fewer research grants would go to university academic teams and more to community-based centres, and social impact measurements would be developed alongside academic ones.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: First, fewer research grants would be attached to academic research teams based in the university but more grants would be given to community-based research centres.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Second, instead of solely using academic impact measurements to evaluate the performance of research, for example, publications in journals and citation indices, social impact measurements will have to be developed to take into account the relevance of applied social science research.

sections.label: Privileging Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage states that the commitment should be long-term and grounded in family and community life, and that Singaporeans should be privileged all else being equal.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One expects this commitment to be a long-term one grounded in family and community life here.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, all else being equal in terms of quality or potential for quality, let us privilege Singaporeans.

sections.label: Consolidated degree certificate reprint
sections.summary: After completing one module, alumni could get a reprint of a consolidated degree certificate under the SUSS brand.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Upon completion of one module, alumni could then get a reprint of a consolidated degree certificate under the SUSS brand.

sections.label: SUSS as sixth AU
sections.summary: The Government's decision to make UniSIM, now SUSS, Singapore's sixth AU is a good decision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, the Government's decision to make UniSIM, now SUSS, Singapore's sixth AU, is a good decision.

sections.label: SUSS main object
sections.summary: SUSS's main object is to provide lifelong learning programmes with a disciplinary focus in the social sciences for adults.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The main object of SUSS will be to "provide lifelong learning programmes, with a disciplinary focus in the social sciences, for adults".

sections.label: SUSS undergrad age
sections.summary: The current age of SUSS' undergrads today is 29 years old, the speaker was told.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The current age of SUSS' undergrads today is 29 years old, I was told.

sections.label: UniSIM financial model
sections.summary: The inherited UniSIM financial model appears entrepreneurial, using primarily part-time faculty to support a large proportion of part-time adult learner undergrads.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The current UniSIM financial model that was inherited appears to be an entrepreneurial model using primarily part-time faculty members to support a large proportion of part-time adult learner undergrads.

sections.label: SUSS KPIs and evaluation
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister how he will evaluate SUSS and measure success of tertiary institutions, urging MOE to invest in SUSS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: SUSS will need to establish a set of KPIs and criteria that reflect its desired positioning in the overall tertiary education landscape.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I, therefore, seek clarification from the Minister on his views on how he is going to evaluate a university like SUSS and, for that matter, how he intends to measure the success and significance of all his tertiary institutions in the future learning landscape.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: SUSS presents an exciting opportunity to paint and deliver the vision of what future learning for Singapore's working adults and Singapore's lifelong learning adults can be.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I strongly urge MOE to seize this opportunity to strengthen the new SUSS, fully invest in it, so that it will take off and it will soar as the very unique provider for a very unique group of learners in a very unique education age.

sections.label: Government education expenditure tripled
sections.summary: Between 1990 and 2000, total Government expenditure on education nearly tripled.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Between 1990 and 2000, total Government expenditure on education nearly tripled.

sections.label: Tertiary spending above other economies
sections.summary: In 2010, Singapore's Government expenditure per tertiary student as a percentage of GDP per capita was 27.4%, above Australia, the US and Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In terms of Government expenditure per tertiary student as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, Singapore's 27.4% in 2010 was above Australia's, the US' and Hong Kong's.

sections.label: NUS and NTU corporatisation
sections.summary: On 21 November 2005, Parliament passed the Corporatisation Bills for NUS and NTU, transforming them into autonomous universities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On 21 November 2005, Parliament passed the Corporatisation Bills for NUS and NTU, which transformed them into autonomous universities.

sections.label: Fee subsidy for part-time programmes
sections.summary: The fee subsidy now stands at 55% for part-time undergraduate programmes at SUSS and the other AUs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One important form of support is the fee subsidy, which now stands at 55% for part-time undergraduate programmes at SUSS and the other AUs.

sections.label: SUSS meets working adults' aspirations
sections.summary: SUSS offers opportunities that meet the aspirations of working adults in a way unique among IHLs in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SUSS offers opportunities which meet the aspirations of working adults in a way unique among IHLs in Singapore.

sections.label: SUSS mixed student study
sections.summary: Working adults and fresh GCE A level and polytechnic graduates can study side by side in SUSS depending on their classes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In SUSS, working adults and fresh GCE "A" level and polytechnic graduates now have a chance to study side by side, depending on the classes they take.

sections.label: SUSS role in economy
sections.summary: All AUs have a unique role in Singapore's future economy, and SUSS will play a particularly challenging role.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: All of the AUs have a unique role in supporting Singapore's future economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With its focus on social sciences from an applied perspective, SUSS will play a particularly challenging role.

sections.label: UniSIM becomes autonomous public institution
sections.summary: UniSIM was a private entity and now comes under MOE jurisdiction as an autonomous public institution.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Change is a constant in our lives and restructuring is also part and parcel of this.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I have a few clarifications pertaining to this Bill Firstly, UniSIM was a private entity before and now comes under the jurisdiction of MOE as an autonomous public institution.

sections.label: Projected student intake numbers
sections.summary: The passage asks what numbers and increments are projected for student intake in the next two to five years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: What kind of numbers and increments are we projecting in terms of student intake in the next perhaps two to five years?

sections.label: UniSIM appeal and pay scheme
sections.summary: UniSIM appeals to adult learners, and a pay as you study scheme is currently available for them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: UniSIM has its appeal to the adult learners as we have heard over and over again today.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Also, there is currently a "pay as you study scheme" which is available for adult learners.

sections.label: Ministry involvement in research agenda
sections.summary: The passage asks how much involvement the Ministry would have in SUSS's research agenda under clause 5.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My third question would be, looking at clause 5, how much involvement would the Ministry have in the research agenda of SUSS?

sections.label: Social services job openings
sections.summary: The social services sector expects about 3,000 job openings over the next two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: All said, the social services sector is expecting some 3,000 job openings over the next two years.

sections.label: SUSS collaboration and law courses
sections.summary: A speaker asks whether SUSS will collaborate with the Ong Teng Cheong Labour Leadership Institute and notes possible family and criminal law courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can I ask if SUSS or the new university will seek to collaborate with the Ong Teng Cheong Labour Leadership Institute so that the students can get a better grasp of studies in Singapore's trade unionism, for example?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Another important programme that SUSS may or will offer are courses in law which focus on family and criminal law.

sections.label: Consideration for mature childcare students
sections.summary: A speaker hopes for consideration for mature students teaching in childcare centres who may lack the required entry qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Next, I hope some consideration can also be given for mature students, that is, those who have been teaching in childcare centres but may not have the requisite educational qualifications to meet the entry requirements.

sections.label: Business-related SUSS programmes
sections.summary: A speaker welcomes strengthening social sciences but notes four of eight SUSS full-time programme fields are business-related.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: While I welcome the move to strengthen the social sciences and to prepare students for socially-related careers, I note that four out of eight fields in SUSS' full-time programmes are business-related.

sections.label: SUSS applications and needed specialists
sections.summary: Press reports show overwhelming SUSS course response, about 62% of applicants are polytechnic students, and more family/criminal lawyers, early childhood practitioners and specialists are needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Press reports show overwhelming response for SUSS' courses as the number of applications received for some courses far exceeds the number of places available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: A report by The Straits Times also mentioned that about 62% of applicants to SUSS are polytechnic students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Right now, there is a need for more family/criminal lawyers, early childhood practitioners and specialists.

sections.label: Third law school at UniSIM
sections.summary: Singapore's third law school was set up at UniSIM last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year, Singapore's third law school was set up at UniSIM.

sections.label: SUSS programme range clarification
sections.summary: MP asks the Minister to confirm whether SUSS's programme offerings will change from those UniSIM offered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There is also some confusion on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And can the Minister clarify if SUSS will continue to offer the same range of programmes UNISIM had offered?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the MOE press release, it did state, and I quote, that "The university will continue to offer the range of programmes that UniSIM had offered previously, targeted at both fresh school leavers and adult learners." However, in the same press release, it also stated that, and I quote, "At the same time, the university will continue to retain a limited offering in other areas, such as business and engineering, especially for adult learners." Can the Minister confirm whether there will changes in the programmes offered and, if so, what are the changes?

sections.label: Affected staff assistance
sections.summary: MP asks the Minister to clarify whether staff are affected and whether they have been offered assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify if there will be affected staff members and whether they have been offered assistance?

sections.label: Adult learner programme reduction
sections.summary: MP asks whether reduced business, accountancy and engineering offerings for adult learners will be compensated by other institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: UniSIM has been the go-to institution for adult learners who prefer the flexibility of acquiring a part-time degree while working full-time.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, with the shift of focus onto programmes which prepare for careers in the social sector, there will be a reduced focus and offerings in areas, such as business accountancy and engineering, for the adult learners.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will this reduction then be balanced or compensated by the other universities or institutions to ensure continued opportunities for adult learners, especially when greater importance is being placed for science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) programmes which are relevant for the current and future-ready jobs?

sections.label: Name change reactions and employment
sections.summary: MP notes mixed reactions to the name and asks about remuneration, benefits, training and upgrading for employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, the name accorded has received a mixed reaction amongst many, including the past and present SIM/UniSIM students.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Those who graduated or are currently pursuing STEM, Finance or Accountancy courses/degree programmes fear that there will not be much prestige and recognition accorded to these programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From the employment perspective, as the sixth AU which comes directly under the purview of MOE, will there be changes to the remuneration and benefit packages of the employees, including training and upgrading, and will it be favourable?

sections.label: No programme change from name
sections.summary: The response states there will be no change to the university's range of programmes because of the name change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In response to Mr Louis Ng, there will, therefore, be no change to the range of programmes offered by the university just because of the name change.

sections.label: Degree certificates equal standing
sections.summary: Degree certificates in UniSIM's and SUSS's names are of equal standing, and re-issuance arrangements exist for alumni.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Despite the change in name, degree certificates issued in UniSIM's name in the past and SUSS's name now and in the future will be considered of equal standing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, in response to Assoc Prof Daniel Goh, SUSS has made arrangements for degree certifications to be re-issued for alumni.

sections.label: SUSS modular courses introduced
sections.summary: SUSS has already introduced around 200 of such modular courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: SUSS has already introduced around 200 of such modular courses.

sections.label: SUSS applied university research role
sections.summary: SUSS, like SIT, will not be a research-intensive university unlike NTU or NUS, though research should be measured by impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked several questions relating to research, that applied and academic research should co-exist and complement each other, that research should be measured by impact rather than just publications, ensure that we can attract world-class talent for research.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: However, starting off as an applied university, SUSS, just like SIT, will not be a research-intensive university, unlike NTU or NUS.

sections.label: Social Science Research Council funding
sections.summary: SUSS can tap the Social Science Research Council funding for applied research, which awarded about $21 million in grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: SUSS, however, can tap on the Social Science Research Council funding for their applied research.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It has recently awarded about $21 million in grants, and the second grant call has recently been issued.

sections.label: SUSS student intake numbers
sections.summary: SUSS currently takes in about 4,000 students into its full-time and part-time programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: SUSS currently takes in about 4,000 students into its full-time and part-time programmes.

sections.label: SUSS fees and financial assistance
sections.summary: Students on subsidised programmes have the same access to Government-supported financial assistance schemes as peers at the AUs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Students on these subsidised programmes have the same access to Government-supported financial assistance schemes, such as bursaries, tuition fee and study loans, as their peers in similar programmes at the AUs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Hence, we do not expect a significant change in the level of the current subsidised fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And in response to Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef, SUSS will also continue to charge fees based on the number of credits a student wishes to take in a semester.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But we intend to improve the resourcing of the university to further strengthen its capabilities in delivering quality education and training to adult learners and fresh school leavers, so that SUSS, as Ms Denise Phua said, can become the best in its field, especially with regard to lifelong learning.

sections.label: Part-time and full-time programme fees
sections.summary: The cost structure for part-time programmes differs from full-time programmes, and students are eligible for tuition grant for one undergraduate qualification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The cost structure for part-time programmes is different from that of full-time programmes, which makes it quite difficult to compare the two.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But both courses under an AU are significantly subsidised, and the fees that a student pays for a part-time course is often less than that of a similar full-time course after subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Because budget is always limited, we need to ensure it can benefit as many Singaporeans as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Hence, students are currently only eligible for tuition grant for one qualification at the undergraduate level.

sections.label: SUSS university transformation agreements
sections.summary: SUSS will work with MOE on new policy and performance agreements with KPIs, after UniSIM subsidies and existing checks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As MOE has been providing subsidies for students pursuing their undergraduate programmes in UniSIM since 2008, the university is already subject to similar checks and balances as the other AUs, such as the Quality Assurance Framework for Universities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But with its transformation into an AU, SUSS will also be working with MOE on new policy and performance agreements that outline a mutually agreed vision and direction for the university and corresponding KPI and success indicators.
